name: TCM & Chinese medicine (category guide)
summary: TCM Practitioners Board–registered physicians for expats — what group medical usually excludes, fertility ‘tiao’ realism, and when TCM is adjunct not substitute for acute care.
body: Only practitioners registered with the TCM Practitioners Board may legally practise Chinese medicine in Singapore — verify the name before you book WeChat referrals. Group hospital plans commonly exclude TCM, herbal medicines, and acupuncture, or reimburse only under a tiny outpatient rider — assume cash until HR confirms a written line. Fertility forums often suggest TCM ‘body tuning’ alongside IVF; treat it as adjunct care with clear stop rules, not a replacement for ART workups or obstetric red flags. Acute chest pain, trauma, and paediatric emergencies still belong in Western A&E first. Ask whether herbs are dispensed in-clinic, how they interact with prescription meds, and whether English consult notes are available for your GP. This is a category guide for regulated TCM access, not an endorsement of any fertility claim or a ranked physician list.
